toml:
# LEO-PNT resilience from received power: the jammer-to-signal (J/S) margin.
#
# A jammer denies a signal when the jammer power it lets through, relative to the signal's
# own received power, pushes the effective carrier-to-noise density (C/N0) below the
# tracking threshold. A low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite is about 20 to 40 times closer than
# a medium Earth orbit (MEO) GNSS satellite, so the same transmitter delivers 26 to 32 dB
# more power, and every dB of received power is a dB of J/S margin.
#
# One wideband (barrage) noise jammer, 40 MHz wide at 1185 MHz, covers GPS L5, Galileo E5a
# and two LEO signals in the same band. Its received power steps up by 5 dB every 10 s
# from -125 dBW at 10 s to -90 dBW at 80 s. The `spectrum` kind's first-loss time of
# each band is where the jammer takes it:
#   gps-l5       interface-document minimum, -157.9 dBW
#   galileo-e5a  interface-document minimum, -155.0 dBW
#   xona-x5      the published minimum received power, -144.9 dBW (arXiv 2509.19551)
#   generic-l    a representative LEO L-band signal at -135 dBW, 1191.795 MHz
# GPS L5 is lost at the -105 dBW step, Galileo E5a at -100 dBW, Xona X5 at -95 dBW; the
# generic signal still tracks at -90 dBW. Received power buys J/S margin dB for dB.
# Received powers are those at the stated minimum; a real pass varies over it (see the
# leo-pass scenarios).
#
# MODELLED: the signal spectra are validated closed forms; the jammer steps and the
# received powers are scenario inputs.
